references.text: When you enter the land and plant trees, this points to the promise of entering the promised land, as also described in Deuteronomy.
The continuation of the law concerning fruit trees, explaining that in the fifth year the fruit may be eaten after it has been dedicated to the Lord.
In the fourth year all the fruit is to be holy, a praise offering to the Lord - this is the direct context for the three-year law.
The term 'uncircumcised' (ערל) is used metaphorically here regarding uncircumcised lips, just as fruit is called 'uncircumcised' in Leviticus.
Refers to planting vineyards and not being allowed to enjoy the fruit as a curse, in contrast to the blessing of following God's laws.
The prophecy about planting vineyards on the mountains of Samaria and enjoying their fruit points to the fulfillment of the promise in the promised land.
The promise to inherit trees that the Israelites did not plant shows God's gift of the land with already established fruit trees.
